title: maptimeDavis: Map Room Tour + Open House
location: Shields Library Map Room, 93 Shields Library
description:
Learn to search the catalog, find & handle maps & air photos, use maps & air photos in GIS software, and use stereoscopes & loupes. See historic campus maps & air photos! Learn about map collection projects & incoming new materials!
 

Speaker: Sheena Campbell & Michele Tobias
 

UC Davis STEM Librarian, Sheena Campbell, provides information literacy instruction to undergraduate and professional students in the STEM fields, offers individualized research support, and identifies resources to enhance the library’s collections. With her background as an artist and historian, Sheena’s research interests focus on the intersection of visual culture, environmental justice, and the history of scientific thought.
 

Michele Tobias is a geospatial data scientist with a background in geospatial methods for ecology. Michele earned her PhD from UC Davis in Geography where she studied California’s sandy beach ecosystem with traditional phytosociological methods and innovative remote sensing tools and was a postdoc at the UC Davis Information Center for the Environment. In her current position as a geospatial data scientist at the UC Davis Library, she applies geospatial tools to new avenues of research across disciplines.
 

Prerequisites: None
 

Software Required: None

description:
join us in celebrating our new library mural, created by undergraduate students in the Mural Workshop (ART 171/CHI 171) in Spring 2026. Drawing on the Chicanx tradition of muralism, the students' creative process centered on community engagement, collective storytelling, and sense of place. Vibrant imagery of students, photos from the library's University Archives, and an oak tree bearing the words “Saber es Poder” (“Knowledge is Power”) are among the elements that explore the library as a space where preservation and empowerment meet. title: Mercy Hawkins: Waltz of Life & Limb
location: Pence Gallery, 212 D Street, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Mercy Hawkins: Waltz of Life & Limb
Exhibit: October 3 – November 6, 2026
Reception: October 9, 6-9 PM (Free) 
Waltz of Life & Limb pairs recent sculptural paintings by artist Mercy Hawkins, with her vibrant, large-scale watercolors on paper. With this work, Hawkins seeks to answer the internal call, to encounter what the body already knows, from our own inner rhythms, heartbeat, and breath, to dancing with wild arms. Her biomorphic shapes, formed of intersecting dots, dashes, and lines, speak to a sensory play of color, light, and movement. Her imagery evokes seed pods, flower buds, or microscopic creatures, immersing the viewer in an all-encompassing perception of nature. 
Artist Talk: Saturday, October 17, 2-3:30 PM (Free)
Mercy Hawkins will speak about the development and trajectory of several bodies of recent work, including its connection to craft. She will also explore the intersection of painting and music. 
Sponsored by HF Richardson

title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection
location: Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis, 254 Old Davis Road, Davis, California, 95616
description: This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.

title: Birds & Bikes
location: Axis Gallery, 625 S St, Sacramento, 95811, United States
description:
Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. 
The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. 
Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop-Up Shop. 
Participating artists include Antonia Price, Sokthea Chan*, Linda Clark Johnson, Nathan Coldwater, Kate Farrall, Sandy Fong Whetstone, Cara Gregor*, Jordin Hinton, Heather Hogan*, Maris Kaplan, Tanya Lieberman, Elise Mahan*, Lo’Vonia Parks, Judy Coates Perez, Samuel Rose, Jenna Savage, Michelle Sharf, and Alex Williams. (* indicated Axis Member)

title: Banned Books Week
description:
Banned Books Week was launched in 1982 in response to a sudden surge in the number of challenges to books in libraries, bookstores, and schools. Held in the last week of September or first week of October, the annual event highlights the value of free and open access to information and brings together the entire book community — librarians, educators, authors, publishers, booksellers, and readers of all types — in shared support of the freedom to seek and to express ideas. 
The next Banned Books Week will be held October 4–10, 2026. The theme of this year’s event is: Let Books Be — Protect the Freedom to Read.

title: Birds & Bikes
location: Axis Gallery, 625 S St, Sacramento, 95811, United States
description:
Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. 
The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. 
Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop-Up Shop. 
Participating artists include Antonia Price, Sokthea Chan*, Linda Clark Johnson, Nathan Coldwater, Kate Farrall, Sandy Fong Whetstone, Cara Gregor*, Jordin Hinton, Heather Hogan*, Maris Kaplan, Tanya Lieberman, Elise Mahan*, Lo’Vonia Parks, Judy Coates Perez, Samuel Rose, Jenna Savage, Michelle Sharf, and Alex Williams. title: Wisdom of Women Symposium - Unstoppable: Power, Investment & the Future of Women’s Professional Sports
location: Mondavi Center (Mondavi) UC Davis Campus
description:
Women & Philanthropy presents the Wisdom of Women Symposium – Unstoppable: Power, Investment & the Future of Women’s Professional Sports 
Join us for a double-gold day featuring an exclusive conversation with two Olympics gold medalists: soccer legend Brandi Chastain and basketball phenom Candace Parker. They will share their wins and challenges – how they have cultivated success as industry leaders, authors and champions for women in all aspects of life. Following, we’ll talk with a panel of Bay Area leaders to continue the conversation about women thriving in a competitive world. 
Brandi Chastain 
Brandi Chastain is an iconic American athlete, a retired soccer player, two-time Olympic gold-medalist, broadcaster and two-time FIFA Women’s World Cup champion. California-born Chastain has had a fantastic career, playing professionally for several major teams, including Shiroki FC in the Japan Women’s Football League, the San Jose CyberRays of the Women’s United Soccer Association, FC Gold Pride of Women’s Professional Soccer, and California Storm of Women’s Premier Soccer League. Between the 1988 and 2004, Chastain played for the U.S. Women’s National Team; it was during this time that the squad won two Olympic gold medals and two World Cups. 
In sports broadcasting, Chastain has worked as a commentator for soccer matches both with NBC Sports during the 2008 and 2012 Summer Olympics and with ABC/ESPN covering Major League Soccer and the 2011 FIFA Women’s World Cup. A champion of girls’ health, Chastain co-founded the Bay Area Women’s Sports Initiative in 2005 with a mission to create programs and partnerships through which women athletes bring health, hope, and wholeness to the community. She is the author of the 2005 book, “It’s Not About the Bra: Play Hard, Play Fair, and Put the Fun Back Into Competitive Sports.” 
Candace Parker 
Candace Parker has already solidified herself as one of the most influential athletes of this generation. After being selected as the No. 1 overall pick in the 2008 WNBA Draft by the Los Angeles Sparks, following a champion career at Tennessee, Parker went on to become the first player to earn WNBA MVP and Rookie of the Year honors in the same season. Over the course of her illustrious career, Parker won three WNBA championship titles, and took home two Olympic gold medals, helping redefine versatility and excellence in women’s basketball. 
In 2026, she was named a headlining inductee into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. Off the court, first and foremost, she is a wife, mother of three children and three dogs. Since retired, she serves as an author, public speaker, activist, entrepreneur, and studio broadcaster for men’s and women’s basketball. Her recent book, “The Can-Do Mindset: How to Cultivate Resilience, Follow Your Heart, and Fight for Your Passion” breaks down her recipe for success which has helped her success on and off the court. 
Also Speaking:
Ryann Greenberg, vice president of guest experience and venue operations, Bay FC 
Ryann Greenberg is vice president of guest experience and venue operations at Bay FC, responsible for delivering world-class experience for players, fans, and partners across the club’s operations. She leads match day operations and guest experience for the club and as a member of the club’s executive leadership team has helped Bay FC quickly establish itself as a commercial powerhouse by leading the NWSL in merchandise sales and finishing in the top five for average home attendance. Building on that business momentum, the club shattered records by drawing a sellout crowd of 40,091 fans to Oracle Park in their second season, establishing the highest single-game attendance record in U.S. women’s professional sports league history. 
Jess Smith, president, Golden State Valkyries 
Jess Smith began her first season as president of the Golden State Valkyries ahead of the team’s inaugural 2025 season. Smith, who has over 18 years of experience in professional sports, oversees all WNBA business operations. Under Smith’s leadership, the Valkyries have built a winning culture on and off the court. During their inaugural season, the Valkyries set all-time WNBA records for both average attendance (18,064) and total attendance (397,408), selling out all 22 regular-season home games. 
Additional speakers to be announced.

Pamela Wu ’95, director of news and media relations, UC Davis Health 
Pamela Wu’s career spans the fields of broadcast journalism, public relations, and communications training.

title: Rotary Club of Davis Centennial Celebration
location: Veterans Memorial Theatre
description:
Rotary Club of Davis to celebrate 100 years of service
The Rotary Club of Davis will mark its centennial with a community celebration from 5 to 8
p.m. Sunday, Oct. 4, at the Davis Veterans Memorial Center.
Founded in 1926 under the auspices of Rotary International, the Rotary Club of Davis has spent
a century combining service, fellowship and civic involvement. The original Davis club is now
one of three Rotary clubs in the city, along with Sunrise Rotary Club of Davis and Sunset Rotary
Club of Davis.
Tickets for the centennial dinner are $45 and include dinner by Simply Satisfied Catering. For
tickets, contact Donna Prebys at 630-803-7954.
Dave Scheiber will serve as master of ceremonies. The evening’s program will include a
presentation on a century of Davis Rotary by Michael Peterson and Jonathan Bayless, a Rotary
trivia contest led by Bruce and Marjorie Hartsough, and remarks about the club’s future from
Prebys, the club’s 2026-27 president.
The club began with 25 charter members and, by the early 1930s, had grown to nearly 30
members. Rotarians met Mondays at noon at the Terminal Cafe at Second and G streets. Early
activities included support for the Boy Scout Cabin, downtown Christmas-tree decorating,
contributions to a University Farm student-loan fund, sponsorship of a Picnic Day float trophy,
and individual assistance through the club’s charity committee.
As Davis and UC Davis expanded during the 1960s, the club developed a more formal approach
to community projects. Its longtime luncheon meetings were held at the Fellowship Hall of
Davis Community Church through the early 1990s.
The 1970s brought several important changes. The club launched its Turkey Barbecue that spring
as a major fundraiser for local projects. Now known as the Rotary Barbecue, the annual Central
Park event continues with Sunrise Rotary as co-sponsor.
Service projects from that era included planting trees and improving landscaping at Davis High
School, where Rotarians created Rotary Grove, and landscaping Davis Community Park with 75
trees along a walkway leading to the pool. The club also began international service in Fiji, first
helping cover freight costs for educational supplies and later funding four years of high-school
tuition for a student there.
By the 1980s, membership grew from about 110 members to 138. The club supported repairs to
the Boy Scout Cabin, built a parking lot at International House and a snack bar at the Little
League field on F Street, and continued its Fiji educational, medical and housing-support efforts.
The club also joined Rotary International’s PolioPlus initiative after it began in 1986.
Through changing times, the Rotary Club of Davis has remained focused on service projects,
community partnerships and fellowship among members. More information is available at
rotaryclubofdavis.com.

description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

title: Author talk by Peter Flax: Why We Ride

description:
Join us for an inspiring and enlightening look at the reasons that make people fall in love with bicycle riding! Author Peter Flax will share his insights into the creation and production of Live to Ride: Finding Joy and Meaning on a Bicycle, his 2024 book which explores the unifying dynamics of bicycle culture.
 

The book argues that everyone who rides—whether they commute, enjoy nature, or race—has more in common than they might realize. Part of the discussion will focus on a section contextualizing the significance of groundbreaking bike lanes constructed decades ago in Davis—and how Flax was aided by photography and documents from our Archives and Special Collections Department.
 

This talk is free and open to all. Please register in advance to reserve your spot.

About the Speaker
Peter Flax is a Los Angeles-based writer and editor who frequently writes about cycling. He is the former editor in chief of Bicycling magazine and was editorial director at Red Bull Media house. His work has been published by dozens of magazines, including Outside, Time, Alta Journal, Men’s Health, and Runner’s World. Live to Ride was his first book. Flax has lived in Los Angeles for 13 years without a car, doing roughly 100,000 miles of bike commuting in that timeframe.

Join over 500 participants from the IA network and the University of California, Davis and Yolo Bioregion community (a geographic and cultural area that includes the cities of Davis, Woodland, Winters, West Sacramento, and surrounding areas) to engage in deep learning, collaboration, and transformative creativity on the theme of Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times. We will activate spaces across the UC Davis campus, in the City of Davis, and at community-hosted site visits. 
Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times calls us to re-story and honor the places, knowledges, relationships, and ecologies that have been made broken through centuries of violence and abandonment, and the current intensifying fear and repression. We know that our communities are tired, and we know that being together revives our collective spirit, giving us the strength and inspiration we need in troubled times. In this moment of upheaval, the 2026 IA National Gathering draws participants to Davis, CA in the spirit of mending the roots of our connections, and to “awaken,” as Buddhist monk and activist Thích Nhất Hạnh teaches, “from the illusion of our separateness.”

title: U.N. "Reboot the Earth" Hackathon
location: Peter J. Shields Library at UC Davis, 167
description:
In partnership with the United Nations, the UC Davis Open Source Program Office (OSPO)  and DataLab will host a "Reboot the Earth" hackathon. Reboot the Earth is a global initiative that addresses local climate and environmental challenges through open source solutions. 

Representatives of local agencies championing each challenge track will serve as subject matter experts; students will also have access to mentors.

 

Who: 

The event is hosted by DataLab and the UC Davis Library, and is open to students of all backgrounds and experience levels, from any university or college. No prior hackathon experience is required—just curiosity and an eagerness to build something that matters. Participants are strongly encouraged to form interdisciplinary teams and include peers from a variety of majors. Each team may have a maximum of five people and has to include at least one UC Davis student.

 

Why:

Contribute to solving a problem in your community

Get experience working on a cross-functional team

Release an open-source productThe winners are invited to UN Open Source Week at United Nations Headquarters in New York! Travel expenses will be covered for the winning team. 

Schedule:

Kickoff Day (October 23)Wrap-up and Judging (October 24) Participation is required for at least part of both days.

 

Learn More:

At UC Santa Cruz's hackathon in November 2025, the winning team, FireForm, built an AI-powered voice-to-text tool that lets firefighters complete required documentation by speaking naturally instead of typing. They continued developing it after the event, and it has since been certified as a United Nations Digital Public Good. 

 

At UC San Diego (May 2026), the winning team created FireLink, an SMS-based platform that delivers wildfire updates to residents with no internet or smartphone required.

 

This Open Access Week event underlines the UC Davis Library’s commitment to open science.

title: U.N. "Reboot the Earth" Hackathon
location: Peter J. Shields Library at UC Davis, 167
description:
In partnership with the United Nations, the UC Davis Open Source Program Office (OSPO)  and DataLab will host a "Reboot the Earth" hackathon. Reboot the Earth is a global initiative that addresses local climate and environmental challenges through open source solutions. 

Representatives of local agencies championing each challenge track will serve as subject matter experts; students will also have access to mentors.

 

Who: 

The event is hosted by DataLab and the UC Davis Library, and is open to students of all backgrounds and experience levels, from any university or college. No prior hackathon experience is required—just curiosity and an eagerness to build something that matters. Participants are strongly encouraged to form interdisciplinary teams and include peers from a variety of majors. Each team may have a maximum of five people and has to include at least one UC Davis student.

 

Why:

Contribute to solving a problem in your community

Get experience working on a cross-functional team

Release an open-source productThe winners are invited to UN Open Source Week at United Nations Headquarters in New York! Travel expenses will be covered for the winning team. 

Schedule:

Kickoff Day (October 23)Wrap-up and Judging (October 24) Participation is required for at least part of both days.

 

Learn More:

At UC Santa Cruz's hackathon in November 2025, the winning team, FireForm, built an AI-powered voice-to-text tool that lets firefighters complete required documentation by speaking naturally instead of typing. They continued developing it after the event, and it has since been certified as a United Nations Digital Public Good. 

 

At UC San Diego (May 2026), the winning team created FireLink, an SMS-based platform that delivers wildfire updates to residents with no internet or smartphone required.

 

This Open Access Week event underlines the UC Davis Library’s commitment to open science.

title: Author Talk: Market Memories Cookbook with Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan (Davis)
location: Blanchard Room, Mary L Stephens Davis Branch Library
description:
The cookbook, which has 92 recipes, arranged by season, also tells the story of how the county’s iconic market evolved as the brainchild of four young Davis people, including co-author Ann M. Evans, with a few farmers selling fruits and vegetables from the back of their pick-ups, to one of the most recognized farmers market in the United States. 

The story is told through personal essays by the co-founders and others with seminal involvement, 32 anecdotal quotes from vendors, shoppers, and elected officials, and a timeline chronicling market highlights over 50 years, as well as an in- memoriam page, commemorating the market vendors who are deceased.

The book is illustrated by Ann and Georgeanne as well, with beautiful pen and ink and watercolor washes for fruit and vegetables and flowers in all the seasons.

title: Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year)
location: Central Park, 301 C St., Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! 
Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. 
Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. 
The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. 
Wednesday Market Details: 

Wednesdays from 3:00–6:00 PM
Central Park in Downtown Davis
Fresh, seasonal produce
Artisan goods and prepared foods
Local farmers and food makers
Family-friendly and open to everyone

Free to attend – shop local and enjoy your Wednesday afternoon at the Davis Farmers Market!

title: Blood on the Clocktower at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
The first Wednesday of every month, we play _Blood on the Clocktower_, a social deduction game in the vein of Werewolf/Mafia/The Resistance, with a few twists!

We'll have a circle of chairs reserved inside Blue Note, near the back, with a Yolo County Board Game Gathering sign on the table. Just say hello, and we'll show you some games, pull some players together, and get to having fun!

We also usually have a few tables of players playing other board games, if social deduction isn't your bag!

Get a feel for Blood on the Clocktower here: https://youtu.be/4sfa8_kNxsQ

description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change. 
  
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance. 
  
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.

title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

title: 2nd Friday ArtAbout – Monthly Downtown Davis Art Walk (Free!)
description:
Join Davis’s beloved 2nd Friday ArtAbout – a free monthly self-guided artwalk coordinated by the Pence Gallery! Every second Friday, stroll downtown Davis to discover fresh exhibits, opening receptions, live music, hands-on activities, and direct chats with local and regional artists at 10+ galleries, co-ops, and businesses. 
Support our vibrant arts scene, uncover unique talent and styles, and soak up the lively energy – ideal for friends, families, dates, or solo adventures. Many venues offer complimentary refreshments like wine and snacks. 
Free – no tickets required! 

Runs approximately 5:00–9:00 PM (venue receptions vary—check the monthly guide for specifics).
Grab the printed guide (with map & details) the week of at the Pence Gallery or participating spots, or download it at pencegallery.org/events/artabout/.

Interested in hosting as a venue, artist, or business? Visit https://pencegallery.org/events/artabout/ to fill out the corresponding forms. Please submit events 3 weeks in advance via the form on the site to be included in the guide and promotions. 
Stay in the loop: facebook.com/davisartabout 
Come celebrate local creativity downtown – see you on the next second Friday! 🎨✨
